stories.headline: A PHP security flaw just took down government sites worldwide
stories.blurb: Governments and companies in Kenya, the Netherlands, and beyond are racing to patch a critical vulnerability in PHP, the programming language that runs roughly 75% of all websites. The scramble left many sites temporarily offline as admins rushed emergency fixes to prevent hackers from exploiting the flaw.
stories.why_it_matters: If you run anything on PHP, you need to patch now — this affects three-quarters of the web.
stories.original_headline: PHP Security Flaw Sets Off Global Rush to Patch, Leaving Websites Offline

stories.headline: Anthropic's new Claude Duet agent can monitor your apps and do your busywork
stories.blurb: Claude Duet is Anthropic's new AI agent that briefs you each morning on what's happening across your connected apps, then watches them all day and pings you only when something needs attention. You can hand it tasks from scheduling meetings to building dashboards or prototyping web apps. It runs in a virtual machine with browser access and asks permission before sensitive actions like payments.
stories.why_it_matters: Another AI agent competing to become your always-on work assistant across all your tools.
stories.original_headline: Anthropic takes on Muse with Claude Duet, its new AI agent

stories.headline: DeepSeek raises $15B two days after US bans its AI from federal agencies
stories.blurb: The Chinese AI lab closed one of the country's biggest funding rounds—backed by battery maker CATL and Tencent—just 48 hours after Washington ordered civilian agencies to remove DeepSeek software over security concerns. The company raised $7B in June and is reportedly eyeing a China IPO next year.
stories.why_it_matters: US restrictions aren't slowing Chinese AI funding—they may be accelerating it.
stories.original_headline: DeepSeek reportedly raises $15B days after US restrictions

stories.headline: Recursive shipped a laptop coding model built mostly by AI
stories.blurb: Flint is a free coding assistant that runs offline on your laptop, using only 2.5 billion parameters at a time. Recursive says its automated research system handled nearly every step of development, letting a small team build the model from scratch in under four months. You can download it now on Hugging Face.
stories.why_it_matters: First real test of AI building better AI, running locally without cloud fees or data leaving your machine.
stories.original_headline: Recursive launches Flint, a laptop coding model it says was largely built by AI

stories.headline: Walmart will let AI agents shop for you while Amazon blocks them
stories.blurb: Starting next month, Walmart lets AI agents browse and buy on its site with your approval — you set spending limits, review purchases separately, and can shut it off anytime. The move uses the Model Context Protocol standard and flips Amazon's approach, which blocked Perplexity and Meta's shopping agents.
stories.why_it_matters: The first major retailer actively building infrastructure for AI agents to shop autonomously.
stories.original_headline: Walmart is inviting AI agents to shop for you

try_this_prompt.title: The hiring regret vaccine
try_this_prompt.prompt: I'm about to hire someone and I'm 80% sure they're right. Describe the candidate in a few sentences below. Now tell me: the specific moment six months in when I'll regret this hire, the yellow flag I'm probably ignoring right now, and the one question I should ask in the final interview that will surface it.
try_this_prompt.tool_hint: Before you extend the offer and spend three months onboarding the wrong person.
